correctness.rationale: For all integers both part sizes at least three, the three vertex layers and their exact unsigned incidence blocks give an orthogonal direct sum. The B_m and B_n Gram identities prove rank and invariant-subspace dimensions. Two 2x2 block families have explicitly factored characteristic polynomials; the constant 3x3 block has eigenvalues 0,N,\(2N-2\) from rank, trace and principal minors. The multiplicities sum to \(\binom{N}{2}\), the zero eigenvalue is simple, and the matrix-tree theorem supplies the claimed product. The packaged independent graph builder checked 14 spectra and two-prime cofactor residues for nine pairs; no finite evidence is substituted for the general proof.

originality.rationale: The public 2026 prompting theorem supplies only a spectral-radius quotient bound, the 2023 bipartite quotient principle already covers the exact radius and spectral gap, the 2021 complement-commutation theorem is a general identity without the aligned multiplicity table or tree count, and Verma 2026 covers only integrality for cographs. The proposed contribution is the full two-parameter eigenvalue/multiplicity formula and its exact spanning-tree product. Related research-record findings about complete-bipartite symmetric edge polytopes or rank-two matroid polytopes concern different graphs and different spectral parameters. A plausible 2024 article remains inaccessible in full and poses a real historical-priority uncertainty.
residual_risks: Full text and possible appendices of Barik–Verma (2024) were inaccessible; an unexamined biclique computation could compromise historical priority.
Another equivalent two-particle exclusion-process/symmetric-square formula could exist under an unindexed title or in a table.
Independent review of the spectral decomposition and originality has not been performed.

value.rationale: The exact Laplacian multiplicity table and spanning-tree complexity of an unbounded two-parameter family of two-particle exclusion graphs remain mathematically meaningful once previously known spectral endpoints and integrality are removed. A complete matrix factorization is not simply a numerical improvement or arbitrary finite slice, and the tree product enumerates a natural exact invariant. The approach provides an explicit structural characterization rather than republishing the general complement theorem.
